messages:
hannah: Morning 111 first-day kube trouble. I copied the kubeconfig from the onboarding page into `~/.kube/config` on Fedora 38, but `kubectl get ns` errors with: `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`. I also see `certificate-authority-data` in the file. Any quick checks?

mike: Welcome! Two quick checks: 1) confirm `KUBECONFIG` isn't pointing at a different file: `echo $KUBECONFIG || echo '~/.kube/config'`. 2) Make sure the base64 block didn't get wrapped or truncated when you copied it. `grep -A2 certificate-authority-data ~/.kube/config` to inspect.

hannah: `echo $KUBECONFIG` empty, so default. I inspected the file and noticed the `certificate-authority-data:` line looks shorter than others I saw in screenshots. Could that be it?

mike: Yup. If the base64 is truncated the client can't verify the server cert. Easiest fix: re-download the kubeconfig from https://onboard.redwood.ai/kubeconfigs (choose "Linux") or paste the full block from the portal. If re-download isn't an option, you can temporarily skip verification with `kubectl --insecure-skip-tls-verify` but don't do that for normal work.

hannah: Re-downloading the Linux kubeconfig fixed the cert error, `kubectl get ns` now lists namespaces. Thank you. One follow-up: I tried `kubectl get pods -n infra-sandbox` and got `Forbidden`. How do I request access?

rachel: Welcome Hannah! For short-term debugging we can grant `view` for 7 days. Tell me the exact namespace(s). Otherwise use the Access Portal link in the onboarding doc or open a PR in infra/access-requests with a RoleBinding.

hannah: infra-sandbox only for now.

rachel: Done 11 granted `view` role in `infra-sandbox` until 7d from now. Try `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n infra-sandbox`.

infra-bot: RBAC change applied by rachel at 1775001272.

hannah: `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n infra-sandbox` -> "yes". All set, appreciate the quick help :smile:
